title: Stability Is Not Evidence: Shrinkage Artefacts in a Pre-Registered Neural Value-at-Risk Study
description:
Code, frozen data snapshots, pre-registration record, execution ledger and manuscript for a pre-registered study of whether anchoring a quantile-loss neural network to a classical Value-at-Risk prior improves one-day-ahead forecasts.

The study produced four apparently well-supported findings and withdrew all four. One fell to a multiplicity correction, one to a power analysis, one to a check of the model's own seed noise, and one — replicated across four runs with a dose–response relationship and a sign test at p = 5.2e-04 — to a scale-matched permutation control costing 28 minutes of validation compute.

This archive contains everything needed to check that claim independently: the sha256 manifest of the frozen ten-year price snapshots (the price files themselves are not redistributed, per the data vendor's terms), the append-only test-touch ledger recording all 1,959 test-set evaluations, the analysis code, 123 tests, and the scripts that regenerate every figure and every number quoted in the paper. No reported number is typed by hand; scripts/refresh_paper_figures.py --check fails if any summary drifts from the result files it claims to summarise.
notes: Every figure and every quoted number is regenerated from the result files by scripts in this archive. The test-touch ledger discloses 1,959 test-set evaluations across 16 asset-level cells and four scoring passes, with zero cells scored only once.
